2791-essays-and-tales.title: Essays And Tales
2791-essays-and-tales.creator: Joseph Addison.
2791-essays-and-tales.description: A book by Joseph Addison.. ament and in many of the outward signs of character; but these two little books will very distinctly show how wholly they agreed as to essentials. For Addison, Literature had a charm of its own; he delighted in distinguishing the finer graces of good style, and he drew from the truths of life the principles of taste in writing.

301-the-ballad-of-reading-gaol.title: The Ballad Of Reading Gaol
301-the-ballad-of-reading-gaol.creator: Oscar Wilde
301-the-ballad-of-reading-gaol.description: A book by Oscar Wilde. Some love too little, some too long,  Some sell, and others buy;  Some do the deed with many tears,  And some without a sigh:  For each man kills the thing he loves,  Yet each man does not die.

arxiv-2101-01674.title: From Three Dimensional Manifolds to Modular Tensor Categories
arxiv-2101-01674.creator: Shawn X. Cui, Yang Qiu, Zhenghan Wang
arxiv-2101-01674.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shawn X. Cui, Yang Qiu, Zhenghan Wang. Using M-theory in physics, Cho, Gang, and Kim (JHEP 2020 , 115 (2020) ) recently outlined a program that connects two parallel subjects of three dimensional manifolds, namely, geometric topology and quantum topology.

arxiv-2109-14614.title: Photometric Analysis of the OGLE Heartbeat Stars Journal: ApJ FNPEAKS (Z. Kołaczkowski, W. Hebisch, G. Kopacki), PHOEBE2 (v2.3; Prša et al. 2016a , Horvat et al. 2018 , Conroy et al. 2020 , Jones et al. 2020 ), emcee (v3.0.2; Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 ), MIST (v1.2; Choi et al. 2016 , Dotter 2016 )
arxiv-2109-14614.creator: Marcin Wrona, Piotr A. Kołaczek-Szymański, Milena Ratajczak, Szymon Kozłowski
arxiv-2109-14614.description: Abstract We present an analysis of 991 heartbeat stars (HBSs) from the OGLE Collection of Variable Stars. The sample consists of 512 objects located toward the Galactic bulge, 439 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, and 40 in the Small Magellanic Cloud.

arxiv-2111-12880.title: Active Learning at the ImageNet Scale
arxiv-2111-12880.creator: Zeyad Ali Sami Emam, Hong-Min Chu, Ping-Yeh Chiang, Wojciech Czaja, Richard Leapman, Micah Goldblum, Tom Goldstein
arxiv-2111-12880.description: Abstract Active learning (AL) algorithms aim to identify an optimal subset of data for annotation, such that deep neural networks (DNN) can achieve better performance when trained on this labeled subset. AL is especially impactful in industrial scale settings where data labeling costs are high and practitioners use every tool at their disposal to improve model performance.

arxiv-2201-05831.title: Monojet search for heavy neutrinos at future Z Z -factories
arxiv-2201-05831.creator: Yin-Fa Shen 1 , Jian-Nan Ding 2 , Qin Qin 1
arxiv-2201-05831.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yin-Fa Shen 1 , Jian-Nan Ding 2 , Qin Qin 1. The existence of heavy neutrinos is the most prominent feature of type-I seesaw-like mechanisms, which naturally explain tiny masses of observed neutrinos. Various experiments have been conducted to search for heavy neutrinos, with meson decays sensitive to heavy neutrinos lighter than B B mesons and high energy collider experiments sensitive to the ones with masses larger than 𝒪 ⁡ ( 0.1 ) \mathcal{O}(0.1) TeV.

arxiv-2303-18139.title: Efficient View Synthesis and 3D-based Multi-Frame Denoising with Multiplane Feature Representations
arxiv-2303-18139.creator: Thomas Tanay, Aleš Leonardis, Matteo Maggioni
arxiv-2303-18139.description: Abstract While current multi-frame restoration methods combine information from multiple input images using 2D alignment techniques, recent advances in novel view synthesis are paving the way for a new paradigm relying on volumetric scene representations. In this work, we introduce the first 3D-based multi-frame denoising method that significantly outperforms its 2D-based counterparts with lower computational requirements.

arxiv-2311-00405.title: Couples can be tractable: New algorithms and hardness results for the Hospitals / Residents problem with Couples Thanks: A preliminary version of this paper appeared in the Proceedings of IJCAI 2024 [ 9 ] .
arxiv-2311-00405.creator: Gergely Csáji, David Manlove, Iain McBride, James Trimble
arxiv-2311-00405.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gergely Csáji, David Manlove, Iain McBride, James Trimble. In this paper, we study the Hospitals / Residents problem with Couples ( hrc ), where a solution is a stable matching or a report that none exists.

arxiv-2311-09891.title: Classification-based detection and quantification of cross-domain data bias in materials discovery
arxiv-2311-09891.creator: Giovanni Trezza, Eliodoro Chiavazzo
arxiv-2311-09891.description: Abstract It stands to reason that the amount and the quality of data is of key importance for setting up accurate AI-driven models. Among others, a fundamental aspect to consider is the bias introduced during sample selection in database generation.

arxiv-2411-18968.title: Perception of Visual Content: Differences Between Humans and Foundation Models
arxiv-2411-18968.creator: Nardiena A. Pratama, Shaoyang Fan, Gianluca Demartini
arxiv-2411-18968.description: Abstract Human-annotated content is often used to train machine learning (ML) models. However, recently, language and multi-modal foundational models have been used to replace and scale-up human annotator’s efforts. This study compares human-generated and ML-generated annotations of images representing diverse socio-economic contexts. We aim to understand differences in perception and identify potential biases in content interpretation.

arxiv-2508-04229.title: Intention Enhanced Diffusion Model for Multimodal Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
arxiv-2508-04229.creator: Yu Liu, Zhijie Liu, Xiao Ren, You-Fu Li, He Kong
arxiv-2508-04229.description: Abstract Predicting pedestrian motion trajectories is critical for path planning and motion control of autonomous vehicles. However, accurately forecasting crowd trajectories remains a challenging task due to the inherently multimodal and uncertain nature of human motion. Recent diffusion-based models have shown promising results in capturing the stochasticity of pedestrian behavior for trajectory prediction.

arxiv-2511-17638.title: Model-to-Model Knowledge Transmission (M2KT): A Data-Free Framework for Cross-Model Understanding Transfer
arxiv-2511-17638.creator: Pratham Sorte
arxiv-2511-17638.description: Abstract Modern artificial intelligence systems depend heavily on large datasets for both training and transferring knowledge between models. Knowledge distillation, transfer learning, and dataset distillation have made such transfers more efficient, yet they remain fundamentally data-driven: a teacher must produce examples, logits, or gradients for a student to learn.

arxiv-2512-21904.creator: Alexander Bednarek
arxiv-2512-21904.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexander Bednarek. This is the first of two papers studying both the geometric structure of Fano fibrations and the application to Kähler-Ricci flows developing a singularity in finite time. Given a Fano fibration which is generated by Kawamata’s theorem from a compact Kähler manifold X X endowed with an ample, rational line bundle L L and non-nef canonical line bundle K X K_{X} , we construct a ( 1 , 1 ) (1,1) -form on the regular part of the base analytic variety which

britannica-1911-espalier.title: Espalier (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-espalier.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-espalier.description: Article 'Espalier' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 9), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. something to rest the spalla or shoulder against; the word is ultimately the same as épaulière, a shoulder-piece), a lattice-work or row of stakes, originally shoulder high, on which fruit trees, shrubs and flowers, particularly roses and creepers, are trained. Espaliers are usually made of larch or other wood, iron and metal rails being too great conductors of heat and cold.

europmc-pmc6097415.title: Abscopal effect of radiotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
europmc-pmc6097415.creator: Liu Y, Dong Y, Kong L, Shi F, Zhu H, Yu J.
europmc-pmc6097415.description: Radiotherapy (RT) is used routinely as a standard treatment for more than 50% of patients with malignant tumors. The abscopal effect induced by local RT, which is considered as a systemic anti-tumor immune response, reflects the regression of non-irradiated metastatic lesions at

pmc-10513317.title: Highlighter: An optogenetic system for high-resolution gene expression control in plants
pmc-10513317.creator: Bo Larsen, Roberto Hofmann, Ines S. Camacho, Richard W. Clarke, J Clark Lagarias, Alex R. Jones, Alexander M. Jones
pmc-10513317.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Optogenetic actuators have revolutionized the resolution at which biological processes can be controlled. In plants, deployment of optogenetics is challenging due to the need for these light-responsive systems to function in the context of horticultural light environments. Furthermore, many available optogenetic actuators are based on plant photoreceptors that might crosstalk with endogenous signaling processes, while others depend on exogenously supplied cofactors. To overcome such challenges, we have developed Highlighter, a synthetic, light-gated gene expression system tailored for in planta function.

pmc-10596479.title: Associations between lifestyle change during the COVID-19 pandemic and mental health in adolescents
pmc-10596479.creator: F Manneville, A Y Omorou, S Bitar, B Lalloué, J Epstein, J O'Loughlin, N Agrinier, L Minary
pmc-10596479.description: BackgroundIt is unclear whether changes in physical activity or sugar consumption during the COronaVIrus Disease (COVID)-19 pandemic relate to later mental health among adolescents. This study identified profiles of change in physical activity and sugar consumption during the COVID-19 pandemic, and estimated associations between these profiles and later anxiety, depression and wellbeing among adolescents.

pmc-10716730.title: Time to Diagnosis and Treatment of Lyme Disease by Patient Race
pmc-10716730.creator: Samuel J. Starke, Alison W. Rebman, John Miller, Ting Yang, John N. Aucott
pmc-10716730.description: This cross-sectional study compares stages at which Lyme disease was diagnosed by race in a specialty clinic in the US. Introduction Early diagnosis of Lyme disease (LD) requires prompt recognition of the erythema migrans (EM) rash and/or viral-like symptoms. Untreated infection can progress to disseminated disease, which is associated with more significant, prolonged morbidity.

pmc-11480056.title: Examining the causal association between moderate alcohol consumption and cardiovascular risk factors in the Taiwan Biobank: a Mendelian randomization analysis
pmc-11480056.creator: Pei-Shan Chien, Tzu-Jung Wong, An-Shun Tai, Yau-Huo Shr, Tsung Yu
pmc-11480056.description: BackgroundThe Mendelian randomization approach uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to study the causal association between the risk factors and health outcomes of interest. We aimed to examine the relation between alcohol consumption and cardiovascular risk factors using two genetic variants as instrumental variables: alcohol dehydrogenase 1B (ADH1B) rs1229984 and aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) rs671.

pmc-12371047.title: Optical emission inventory of carbonaceous aerosol from the residential sector in China
pmc-12371047.creator: Lu Zhang, Yaojie Li, Xinlei Liu, Jin Li, Guofeng Shen, Shu Tao
pmc-12371047.description: The residential sector in China is a major contributor to light-absorbing carbonaceous aerosols, including black carbon and brown carbon, which have significant impacts on climate change. This study developed a province-level inventory of optical emissions of carbonaceous aerosols from the residential sector in China from 1960 to 2019.

pmc-12450285.title: The Need for Telehealth Education in the Medical School Curriculum
pmc-12450285.creator: Madilyn Carney, Mary E Thornton, Kavya Avancha, James R Nolin, Julia Alexander
pmc-12450285.description: The need for telehealth increased significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic and has continued to be a popular method for patients to consult with their physicians. As telemedicine has expanded and become an integral part of a physician's daily practice, a question arises: how does one translate an in-person visit to a virtual one?

pmc-12452337.title: Neck Pain in Dental Education: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Neck Strength Differences
pmc-12452337.creator: Manuel B Almeida, Marion Moreira, Paula Moleirinho-Alves, Raúl Oliveira, Guglielmo Duranti
pmc-12452337.description: This study aimed to investigate if there are differences in neck strength between dental students in their fourth and fifth years, with and without neck pain. Neck muscle strength was assessed in flexion, extension, and lateral flexion to both sides using a handheld dynamometer while participants performed maximum voluntary isometric contractions with a make test procedure.

pmc-12586902.title: S‐Methyl‐l‐Cysteine Sulfoxide: A Hidden Layer of Defences Against Herbivorous Insects in Brassicaceae
pmc-12586902.creator: Laura Bellec, Célia Le Maire, Nathalie Marnet, Chrystelle Paty, Anne‐Marie Cortesero, Maxime R. Hervé
pmc-12586902.description: Plants defend themselves against herbivorous insects through diverse morphological and biochemical traits. Non‐protein amino acids (NPAAs) are an important component of the plant metabolome, although their defensive function remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigated the role of S‐methyl‐l‐cysteine sulfoxide (SMCSO), a sulphur‐containing NPAA accumulated in Brassicaceae, in mediating plant defence against herbivorous insects.

pmc-12843472.title: Genetic Markers of Methotrexate Treatment Failure in Psoriasis
pmc-12843472.creator: Maria N. Vikhreva, Lavrenty G. Danilov, Andrey A. Martynov, Olga A. Levashova, Svetlana N. Tuchkova, Sherzod P. Abdullaev, Karin B. Mirzaev, Andrey S. Glotov, Oleg S. Glotov, Dmitry A. Sychev
pmc-12843472.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Pharmacogenetic markers associated with the need to switch patients from methotrexate (MTX) to biologic agents in moderate-to-severe psoriasis remain insufficiently studied. The pharmacokinetics of MTX depend on the individual characteristics of the patient, as well as on the function of specific transporters and enzymes involved in its absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination; therefore, polymorphisms in genes encoding these proteins may be considered pharmacogenetic predictors of MTX intolerance or insufficient efficacy.

pmc-13066847.title: Y-shaped pulmonary artery in modified Fontan surgery: a multimodality imaging case
pmc-13066847.creator: Rui Lv, Zhenglun Alan Wei, Xiaona Lin, Chenze Tian, Bin Qiao
pmc-13066847.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Case presentation Figure 1 illustrates the surgical details, encompassing ligation of the main pulmonary artery (MPA) (Figure 1A,1B), the right SVC (RSVC) was disconnected and anastomosed to the right PA (RPA); the innominate vein (IV) was disconnected and anastomosed to the left PA (LPA) as left SVC (LSVC), and anastomosis was performed of the conduit with the MPA and inferior vena cava (IVC). Notably, in this case, the PA diameter was within expectation, and no PA augmentation was performed.

pmc-13300019.title: Patient-Centred Communication and Behavioural Guidance: An Exploratory Evaluation of the Trainer–Doctor Model in Dental Practice
pmc-13300019.creator: Lucian Josan, Elena Gabriela Strete, Alina Ormenișan, Ioana Cristina Talpos-Niculescu, Diana Marian, Andreea Salcudean, Ana Gabriela Seni, Iustin Olariu

pmc-13351314.title: The Relationship Between Levels of Greenery and Perceived Clinical Signs of Non‐Communicable Diseases in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13351314.creator: Yao Kouassi Kan Théodore, Wandan Eboua Narcisse
pmc-13351314.description: ImportanceUrban green spaces may reduce the prevalence of non‐communicable disease (NCD) symptoms by mitigating environmental risk factors such as pollution and stress. However, evidence from African cities remains limited.ObjectiveTo evaluate the association between levels of urban greenery and the perceived prevalence of clinical signs of non‐communicable diseases in selected municipalities of Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

pmc-13356782.title: Acute kidney injury in children and adolescents with diabetic ketoacidosis managed with aggressive initial volume resuscitation
pmc-13356782.creator: Danielle Saad Nemer Bou Ghosn, Thais Della-Mana, Isabel de Siqueira Ferraz, Claudio Schvartsman, Sylvia Costa Lima Farhat
pmc-13356782.description: Highlights•Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a common complication of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), and it may lead to long-term kidney compromise.•Treatment of DKA with a more aggressive initial fluid therapy is potentially safe and might be associated with renal outcome.•Hyperchloremia associated with a more aggressive initial fluid therapy with NaCl 0.9% in DKA was not found.

pmc-13396632.title: Healthcare professionals’ experiences of telehealth adoption in palliative care: A cross-sectional survey
pmc-13396632.creator: Ann Kirby, Donal Griffin, Ciara Heavin, Fiona Kiely, Frances J. Drummond, Ciara McGrath
pmc-13396632.description: Background:Research has revealed a dramatic rise in the adoption of telehealth by healthcare professionals (HCPs). Limited evidence exists focusing solely on HCPs’ adoption and use of telehealth in palliative care and lacks nuance about when and how telehealth is clinically appropriate.

pmc-13401152.creator: Xinyuan Wu, Jingrao Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Henry K Chu, Xiaolan Chen, Pingting Zhong, Bowen Liu, Mingguang He, Danli Shi

pmc-13500321.title: Rezvilutamide combined with ADT in an HIV-positive patient with high-volume mHSPC on efavirenz-based antiretroviral therapy: a case report
pmc-13500321.creator: Heng Zhang, Tailin He, Zhiyuan Li, Yujie Gao, Yan Li, Yundie Zhou, Haifeng Wang
pmc-13500321.description: This case report describes a patient with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), high tumor burden, and concurrent HIV infection receiving continuous efavirenz (a potent CYP3A4 inducer), who was treated with an intensified regimen based on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) combined with the novel androgen receptor inhibitor rezvilutamide.

pmc-13585483.title: Salt Intake and Kidney Outcomes in Older Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Stage‐Specific Cohort Study
pmc-13585483.creator: Hiroaki Miyauchi, Tatsuhiko Azegami, Takashin Nakayama, Chisato Mitsue, Hirotaka Shibata, Kaori Hayashi
pmc-13585483.description: AimIn patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), salt restriction has been shown to lower blood pressure and proteinuria and to provide kidney protective effects. However, the benefit of salt restriction in older adults with CKD remains unclear, particularly in advanced stages.

pmc-13679355.title: Prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in rural India: a cross-sectional study in the APCAPS cohort
pmc-13679355.creator: Jagannadha Rao Basa, Kanokporn Pinyopornpanish, Poppy AC Mallinson, Papangkorn Inkeaw, Kanokwan Kulprachakarn, Judith Lieber, Santosh Kumar Banjara, Hemant Mahajan, Teena Dasi, Santhi Bhogadi, Srivalli Addanki, Gowri Iyer, Anoop SV Shah, Om Kurmi, Sureshkumar Kamalakannan, Sanjay Kinra, Chaisiri Ang
pmc-13679355.description: BackgroundDementia poses a growing public health challenge in India. Despite this, epidemiological data on the condition remain largely restricted to adults >60 years of age, despite the convergence of urbanisation-driven cardiometabolic risks and socioeconomic disadvantage in rural India potentially accelerating dementia onset.
